newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-GARNETT, GATLING NAMED WESTERN CONFERENCE ALL-STARS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-GARNETT, GATLING NAMED WESTERN CONFERENCE ALL-STARS.

text.p: Minnesota Timberwolves forward Kevin Garnett and Dallas Mavericks forward Chris Gatling were named Wednesday as replacements on the Western Conference team for Sunday's All-Star Game in Cleveland.
The duo replace Houston Rockets guard Clyde Drexler (pulled hamstring) and Los Angeles Lakers centre Shaquille O'Neal (sprained right medial collateral ligament).

The 20-year-old Garnett becomes the second-youngest All-Star in NBA history, behind only Magic Johnson, who was three months younger when he played in 1980. Garnett is averaging 16.4 points, 8.1 rebounds and 2.52 blocked shots in 42 games this season.

Garnett, who skipped college to enter the NBA Draft, was the fifth overall selection in 1995 out of Farragut Academy in Chicago. He earned second team All-Rookie honours last season after averaging 10.4 points and 6.3 rebounds a game.

Gatling leads the Mavericks in scoring (19.0 ppg) and rebounding (7.7 rpg) and is sixth in the league in field goal percentage (53.3) despite being used as a sixth man and averaging around 26 minutes a game.
Gatling, signed to a five-year contract last June, was suspended for one game last week for feuding with Dallas coach Jim Cleamons over playing time.

Seattle forward Detlef Schrempf replaced Houston's Charles Barkley (sprained ankle) on the West squad on Tuesday. On the Eastern Conference roster, New York Knicks centre Patrick Ewing (shoulder) may be replaced as well.
